subject: BUG-090 resolution track: unattributed actor cleared 4 pool bindings -- integrity anomaly, not a capacity question
description: Split out of the binding-reclaim discussion per Nancy 2026-08-02: 'BUG-090 is an unattributed actor mutating binding state, with no credential path even confirmed to explain how. That's an integrity anomaly, not a capacity question, and it doesn't go away because you decided not to reclaim slots.' Frank ruled the reclaim question itself do-nothing/add-slots-if-pressured (2026-08-02, adopting the joint recommendation), so THIS item carries only the anomaly. Known: 4 bindings cleared 08-01/08-02, exactly the 4 a dry run had named; claim_service suppresses request logging (log_message, claim_service.py:592) and journalctl -u openstack-bridge holds 65 start/stop lines only, so no binding history exists; Keystone's own log lives on the openstack-stage1 VM which eq1 has no key for. Candidate steps: (1) get VM shell access via bc2 vm-credentials.txt and pull the Keystone access log for the window; (2) add minimal claim/unbind event logging to claim_service (design question: the logging suppression was deliberate -- check why before reversing); (3) enumerate every credential path that CAN clear hexworth_uid and test which were live that window. See BUG_TRACKER.md BUG-090 (line ~155) and _docs/operations/evidence/pool-sweep-2026-08-02.json.
